extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: The Natural Questions corpus is a question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or marks null if no long/short answer is present. It consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations, 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development, and 7,842 examples with 5-way annotations sequestered as test data.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries of 8 words or more issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time, filtered by heuristic syntactic and lexical rules. Filtered questions were submitted to Google search, and kept if a Wikipedia page was in the top 5 search results. The (question, Wikipedia page) pairs were then provided to human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google search engine query logs (real anonymized, aggregated queries) and Wikipedia pages retrieved via Google search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries of 8 words or more issued by multiple users within a short timeframe were sampled using five heuristic filters based on initial wh-words, auxiliary verbs, categorical noun phrases (identified using Hearst patterns), and part-of-speech tags/entities (from Google's Cloud NLP API) to discard non-questions while retaining complex questions. Queries without a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators used a custom interface to complete a three-stage decision process: (1) Question Identification: judge whether the question is good (fact-seeking) or bad without seeing the document; (2) Long Answer Identification: for good questions, select the earliest HTML bounding box (paragraph, table, list item, or list) containing enough information to infer the answer, or mark 'no answer' (null); (3) Short Answer Identification: for examples with long answers, select the entity/entities answering the question, mark boolean yes/no, or flag no short answer possible.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluated through post hoc expert consensus review across 139 examples (categorized as Correct, Correct but debatable, or Wrong) finding 90% long answer precision and 84% short answer precision. Disagreements and variability were studied using 25-way annotations on 302 examples, showing strong correlation between annotator agreement rates and correctness, as well as multiple valid text locations and span boundaries.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training data (307,373 examples), 5 for development data (7,830 examples) and test data (7,842 examples), and 25 for a study subset of 302 examples
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A pool of around 50 annotators; average annotation time of 80 seconds
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google's Cloud NLP API (used for part-of-speech tagging and entity recognition during query filtering)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The test data (7,842 items with 5-way annotations) is sequestered for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The choice of Wikipedia as the sole source of evidence documents may introduce stylistic or topical biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Excludes queries beginning with 'how to', queries shorter than 8 words, and evidence documents outside Wikipedia. Short answer boundaries and long answer locations exhibit genuine ambiguity and subjectivity across humans.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (validation), and testing benchmark for open-domain question answering and natural language understanding research.
